questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Experiencing what studying in another country is like and have every academic aspect be in English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, but I would prefer a formal introduction to my university instead of having to explore the campus on my own

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a student advisor who was very helpful if I had any questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. I paid to use websites for finding an apartment/room, but eventually I found something through a Facebook group.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very very expensive, but that goes for most of Edinburgh. I enjoyed staying approximately 30 minutes form campus and can recommend not living much further away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very long progress and it seemed like the systems didn't communicate very well even though there should be potential for a more uniform approach as a EU program

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to show up at the student advisor office and fill out a short formula and then we had to make a formal registration where we had to bring our passport

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study abroad administration team at my university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took some time as I decided to change one subject in the introduction week, but it wasn't a problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it is a long process so to be patient

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two 3rd year courses and one 2nd year course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching differed between the courses at University of Edinburgh so it is hard to say, but in genereal I think there is more group work at my host institution and I also found the length of the classes to be impactful. I thought it was nice to only have 50 minutes of lecture as you perceive information better, but I also didn't get the opportunity to socialize with my classmates in a break.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of Health and Healing
Social life and climate change
Himalayan Ethnography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all my courses, but especially enjoyed Himalayan Ethnography because the lecturers are very sweet and engage with the students a lot. It was nice to look a region from many different anthropological perspectives and see how they also intertwine

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different activities, something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Signing up for a society of your interest, but just exploring the city and meeting new people can also be enough in itself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take small trips around the city and perhaps a trip to Glasgow or some of the surrounding towns. Also I really enjoyed all the free museums

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I feel like it is mostly done in societies/sport clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any at the moment

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
That it is a very expensive city to live in
That it is a very nice city and that you settle in very quickly 
That the courses there are interesting

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: My only regret is buying a transport subscription as I just walked everywhere, otherwise I can't really think of anything

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know Edinburgh and experiencing studying in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The short reading holiday/preparation time for the exams and the cost of living

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
